name: worldcup2026
description: Fast, ad-free World Cup 2026 archive — every result, the full knockout bracket, official highlights and 96 years of World Cup history. A single static page on GitHub Pages.

paragraphs: 🏆 Spain won the 2026 World Cup — 1–0 (a.e.t.) against Argentina in the final at MetLife Stadium, 19 July 2026.

The tournament is over, and the site is now its permanent archive: every result, the full knockout bracket, official highlights and 96 years of World Cup history. Nothing on it changes any more — the live scores, goal alerts and the scheduled jobs behind them were retired after the final (see Archive mode).

Every World Cup I just wanted two simple things: to see when each match kicks off in my own time zone, and to add the ones I care about to my calendar — without wading through cluttered, ad-heavy sites to piece it together. I couldn't find anything that did just that, cleanly, so I built it. This is that project: a fast, ad-free, no-tracking companion for World Cup 2026. It's a one-person passion project. 🙌
features: The Highlights tab lists every finished match (newest first) automatically — no upkeep needed. By default each match links out to a YouTube search for that fixture's highlights.

Commit/push and that match shows the embedded clip instead of the search link. Availability depends on the video's region settings — some clips are geo-restricted by broadcast rights, which the page can't change.

requirements.text: 🗣️ Fan wall — leave a public comment, no account needed; every submission is held for review and only appears after the admin approves it (rate-limited, link-free, spam-capped).
Ad-free, no accounts, no money handled.

It needs no API key: fetchscores.py reads this project's own public Worker route and ESPN's public scoreboard, preferring whichever is fresher, and refuses to write a snapshot that would drop an already-finished match.
This needs paid/third-party accounts (API-Football, Cloudflare, OneSignal), so it isn't part of the basic clone — see The live layer.
You don't need to write any code, and you don't need an API key — upload these files and turn two switches on.
Minute-by-minute scores, match stats, the event timeline, line-ups, and push alerts are powered by a Cloudflare Worker rather than the GitHub Action, because they need a paid/real-time feed.
